newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Three groups compete for Moldova GSM licence.
newsitem.headline: Three groups compete for Moldova GSM licence.

text.p: Three groups, involving partners from France, Turkey, Russia, Ireland and Romania, will compete for the licence to operate a Global System Mobile (GSM) communication network in Moldova, officials said on Tuesday.

"The winner will have to invest from $25 to 40 million to set up GSM mobile telephony in Moldova. The local partner must hold at least a 35 percent stake in the future joint venture," Communication Minister Ion Casian told a news conference.

Turkey's Turkcel has joined the local Posta Moldovei company to bid. Russian-Irish group, News Communications, chose Moldova's Technical Center for Radio and Television as its partner. France Telecom united its efforts with Romanian Mobifon, Moltelecom and Mobile Moldovan Telephone.
Casian said the tender committee would announce the winner by May 17. It would take another six to eight months to launch the network.
The technical standard stipulates a four-year period to bring in a phased coverage of Moldovan territory with the GSM network, including not less than 17 percent in the first year.
